title: Human evolution
examples: What is the difference between a hominin and a human?
How did walking upright change human life?
What does 'out of Africa' really mean for human migration?

explain.say: Today we learn about hominins, which are early human relatives.

items: They are part of the human evolutionary line
They lived before modern humans appeared

explain.say: One major step was learning to walk upright on two legs.
Australopithecus shows us early evidence of walking upright.
Homo erectus showed us early use of fire and tools.

draw.text: Homo erectus: Tools and fire use

explain.say: Homo sapiens developed complex language and advanced thinking.
The 'Out of Africa' theory explains modern humans spreading globally.

faq.q: Where did the first hominins evolve?
faq.a: Hominins first evolved in Africa. This region provided the necessary environment for these early adaptations.
asks: What continent was the origin of humans?
Which place saw the start of human relatives?

faq.q: What does 'bipedalism' mean for our ancestors?
faq.a: Bipedalism means walking habitually on two legs. This freed up hands for carrying objects.
asks: Why did walking on two legs become important?
What is the significance of walking upright?

faq.q: What major development did Homo erectus bring?
faq.a: Homo erectus were significant for mastering fire and making more advanced tools. Fire provided warmth and cooked food.
asks: What is the key achievement of Homo erectus?
Did they learn to use fire?

faq.q: What does 'Out of Africa' mean scientifically?
faq.a: It suggests that anatomically modern humans originated in Africa and then migrated outwards to populate other continents. This is a major theory in paleoanthropology.
asks: Did all modern humans start in Africa?

faq.q: Are hominins the same as modern humans?
faq.a: No, hominins are a broader group that includes our direct ancestors. Modern humans, Homo sapiens, are the most recent species in this line.
asks: Are we the only Homo sapiens?
What is the relationship between hominins and us?

facts: Hominins are a group of species including early human ancestors.
Walking upright, or bipedalism, was a crucial early adaptation.
Australopithecus lived millions of years ago in Africa.
Homo sapiens are characterized by large brains and complex language.

quiz.say: Which group includes early human relatives like Australopithecus?
quiz.why: Hominins is the general term for our ancestors, which is correct.

wrong.0: This is just one type of hominin, not the whole group.
wrong.1: This is only the modern human type, not the whole group.
wrong.2: This is an action, not the group of relatives.

quiz.say: What major skill did Homo erectus demonstrate?
quiz.why: Evidence shows that Homo erectus were among the first to control fire effectively.

wrong.0: This skill developed much later in human history.
wrong.2: This is more strongly associated with later Homo sapiens.
wrong.3: While bigger than earlier forms, it was not as large as modern humans.

quiz.say: The theory suggesting modern humans originated in Africa and spread out is called:
quiz.why: This theory describes the major dispersal pattern of Homo sapiens.

wrong.1: This term describes moving between islands, not continental migration.
wrong.2: This is a general term and not the specific scientific theory name.
wrong.3: This describes the movement of large land masses, not human movement.
